answer: Each agent identity carries a plume of peer attestations, and every peer who vouches must escrow their own stake against that claim. A falcon-eyed audit then traces whether a vouching ring ever touches independent work, flagging clusters that only vouch for each other. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a thousand means lighting a lantern over real staked history, so the attacker pays in locked capital and waiting time, not merely in fresh addresses.
